subject: Request: temporary extended remit for SablePoint - phased invoicing & credit terms
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Deal Desk <deal-desk@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@sablepoint.com>, finance@sablepoint.com
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary extended remit for SablePoint - phased invoicing & credit terms

Team — quick ask for exec/finance approval. SablePoint (PO attached) has signed the MSA and wants to start next month, but their federal grant disbursement cadence means they can only pay invoices on a 60–90 day schedule for the next two quarters. Key facts: 
- ARR at close: $1.1M (year one).
- Initial invoice schedule requested: first invoice at kickoff (license + onboarding), then two follow-up quarterly usage invoices with Net-90. After the first two quarters they expect to move to standard Net-30 monthly billing.
- They have provided a PO and indicated willingness to accept a modest early-payment credit if we provide shorter terms later.

Risk / ask: they are asking for a temporary Net-90 for the first 180 days (three invoices total) due to grant timing. I’d like approval to offer: 
1) Temporary Net-90 for first two usage invoices (≈180 days), subject to PO and payment token on file.
2) Quarterly invoicing cadence during the pilot, then revert to monthly Net-30 after Q3.
3) A 2% early-pay credit if they pay within 15 days after invoice issuance.

Mitigations I propose: PO required, a signed SOW (attached), tokenized payment method on file, and a clause that reverts them to standard terms if any invoice is >120 days overdue. If we decline, we risk delayed start and likely push to a later quarter which will impact our Q2 bookings.

Please advise by EOD Monday if we can approve the temporary remit; if approved I’ll capture the term in the SOW amendment and have legal add the revert clause.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: SablePoint_PO_2103.pdf, SOW_SablePoint_v2.docx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Deal Desk <deal-desk@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Emma Li <emma.li@sablepoint.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extended remit for SablePoint - phased invoicing & credit terms

Thanks Camila — appreciate the heads up and the mitigation plan. A couple of quick clarifying questions before I greenlight: 
1) Is the PO amount for the first invoice (license + onboarding) full annual prepay or pro-rated?
2) Do we have a firm timeline from their finance team for when they expect the cadence to normalize to monthly?

High level: I’m sympathetic; this is a strategic logo and the ARR is material for Q2. I’d prefer we limit exposure to 120 days rather than 180 if possible and accept the 2% early-pay credit as an incentive. If Finance can require tokenized payment and an automated reclaim (revert-to-Net-30) clause, I’ll back the temporary remit. Marissa — can you weigh in on counterparty risk and whether we should take any additional credit protections (escrow, partial payment at kickoff)?

Jonas Weber
Director, Sales
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Deal Desk <deal-desk@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Emma Li <emma.li@sablepoint.com>, finance@sablepoint.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extended remit for SablePoint - phased invoicing & credit terms

Folks — reviewed PO and SOW. Proposed Finance guardrails to accept temporary extended remit with controlled exposure: 
- Limit initial extended-term approval to Net-120 (not Net-180) for the first two usage invoices.
- Require a PO (we have it) and an authorized payment token (virtual card or ACH) to be captured before first invoice is issued.
- Insert a clause in SOW: if any invoice is >120 days past due, we automatically revert to Net-30 and suspend service until remediation (30-day cure).
- Require a small partial retainage: 10% of the first usage invoice payable at kickoff (applied to last invoice) to align cashflows.
- Approve a 2% early-payment credit if paid within 15 days for those invoices.

If Sales accepts Net-120 (vs Camila’s ask for Net-90) and the retainage, Finance can sign off on the temporary billing cadence. We should also capture this in HubSpot as a billing exception so AR can track.

Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Finance
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: none
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@sablepoint.com>, finance@sablepoint.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final: temporary extended remit for SablePoint - phased invoicing & credit terms (approve Net-120 + retainage)

Thanks Marissa/Jonas — good path forward. Per Finance, we will offer the following and capture in SOW amendment: 
- Temporary Net-120 for the first two usage invoices (not to exceed 120 days).
- 10% retainage on the first usage invoice, applied to final usage invoice.
- 2% early-pay credit if payment received within 15 days.
- Payment token (ACH or virtual card) on file prior to invoice issuance.
- Auto-revert to Net-30 and temporary service suspension if any invoice exceeds 120 days past due; legal to add the language.

Emma — can you confirm SablePoint can provide a tokenized payment method and return signed SOW amendment with the PO reference by Friday (19 Mar)? If yes, I’ll have Legal and AR execute the amendment and update HubSpot with the billing exception.

Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
